title: Launch lock, process adoption, drain and restart reconciliation
description: Objective: everything between an activation grant and a proven-terminal or reconciled attempt for one Claude node. SPIDR child 2 of 4, split from task-312c1de3c76a4f1dbd8da5c34e629b0e per human-approved 4-child decomposition 2026-08-08 (coarse split: lock/adoption/observation AND cancel/drain/restart deliberately share this task). Design authority: pinned design lines 798 (launch lock, bootstrap credential, duplicate delivery, SUSPECT), 786-787 (reconciliation table), 382/568 (drain on invalidation/remove), 336 (lifecycle). Deliverable: launch-lock protocol records (OS-exclusive lock identity, one-time bootstrap credential registration — lock/credential facts are caller-supplied observations, no syscalls); duplicate delivery adopts the registered process or exits before provider launch; process observation intake over caller-supplied EXITED{code}|SIGNALLED{signal}|UNOBSERVED bound to the adapter's claude-observation and claude-cancel-reconcile outcome shapes; uncertain ARMED/lock state becomes SUSPECT and is never auto-relaunched; the design-786/787 reconciliation: pre-activation intents with every resource proven absent/released are atomically tombstoned with lease/slot fenced-released, budget settled, attempt terminalized by strongest typed reason (RELEASED additionally requires an exact safe handoff); any active/unknown resource forces attempt DRAINING with capacity/NodeRun hold retained until adapter reconciliation, then strongest disposition; restart reconstruction re-derives exactly one legal state from durable records, never a premature terminal. NOT in scope: real OS spawn/job-object/lock syscalls (port-shaped observations; OS wiring is a later task), daemon services (child 3), seeded race harness (child 4), Codex, multi-node. Hard dependencies: Effect intent lifecycle and one-use activation gate (task-2580a578, child 1) for intent records and grant shapes; Claude runtime adapter (task-5ff2b39d, DONE) for observation/cancel-reconcile shapes. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/supervisor/** additions and focused tests (do not rewrite child 1's files; extend). Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: Duplicate delivery with a registered process ADOPTS it (same process identity in the outcome) and without a registration EXITS before provider launch; both arms asserted with their stable codes, and the duplicate-delivery outcome matrix asserts set-equality so a blind-relaunch outcome kind cannot exist unnoticed.
Uncertain ARMED or lock state maps to SUSPECT with a stable code; no SUSPECT or UNKNOWN state can yield a launch grant, asserted against the production surface.

Every design-786/787 reconciliation row has a fixture: all-resources-proven-released terminalizes by strongest typed reason in one step; any active/unknown resource yields DRAINING with capacity held until adapter reconciliation; the row list is asserted so a sweep generating zero rows fails.

Restart reconstruction over seeded pre-crash states lands each in exactly one legal post state (asserted outcome set), never a premature terminal label; RELEASED requires an exact safe handoff and its absence is a distinct refusal.
The focused runner typecheck and test command exits 0 and only explicitly owned paths are staged and committed.
taskRails: Follow pinned design lines 798/786-787/382/568; process termination is best-effort, fencing is authoritative — no post-activation business mutation may be accepted even while DRAINING.
No child_process, spawn, kill, Date.now, or Math.random — all OS facts are caller-supplied observations; uncertainty stays SUSPECT or UNKNOWN and never gains authority.
Do not add package dependencies; mirror foreign shapes structurally with pinned version literals.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400. Commit by explicit pathspec only.
Assert the reason code and refusing layer; mutation-verify failure paths at the mechanism's single source.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/runner/src/supervisor/drain-reconciliation.ts to green. It resolves one row of the step-5 table from (attempt slice state, effect state, resource facts, optional ClaudeReconciliation) and returns a frozen outcome: either TERMINALIZED carrying the strongest typed reason and, for RELEASED, the exact safe handoff it required, or DRAINING carrying what stays held — capacity and the NodeRun hold — until adapter reconciliation. Resource facts are caller-supplied classifications (PROVEN_RELEASED | ACTIVE | UNKNOWN); ACTIVE and UNKNOWN both force DRAINING, and the UNKNOWN arm is the one that must never be optimistically collapsed into released — epic rail 4 keeps unverifiable evidence at UNKNOWN with no authority. An input matching no table row refuses DRAIN_ROW_NOT_ADMITTED rather than falling through to a default, and a reconciliation that leaves a resource unaccounted refuses DRAIN_RESOURCE_UNRECONCILED. Disposition upgrades read the strength order exported by drain-table.ts and refuse DRAIN_DISPOSITION_NOT_MONOTONIC on any attempted downgrade — monotonicity is enforced at this single source so step 9 can mutate it here and see red. Consume the lifecycle's MUST_DRAIN arm rather than re-deriving when a drain is required; it is already a distinct LifecycleOutcome kind, not a refusal. Target under 250 lines; split before 400.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN: 84/84 in drain-reconciliation.test.ts; typecheck exits 0.

SPLIT THREE WAYS to hold the 250 target: drain-reconciliation.ts 227 (row match + the five dispositions), drain-disposition.ts 107 (the monotonic DrainDisposition), drain-fence.ts 63 (the design-568 fence + the MUST_DRAIN bridge). Dependency direction is one-way with no re-export facade — the test imports each surface from the file that owns it — so step 9's mutation drill has exactly one place to poison per mechanism, which was the step's stated reason for centralising monotonicity.

Monotonicity is enforced at ONE source, `isMonotonicDisposition` in drain-disposition.ts, and it checks BOTH halves: the stored strongest reason really is the highest-ranked member of its own reason set, AND the terminal target is that reason's target. Two halves because a target edited alone would retarget the safe boundary while the reason set still looked untouched — the 49-pair sweep would never see it. A disposition that fails either check is REFUSED rather than repaired: silently recomputing the strongest reason would erase the evidence that something downgraded it.

Design fidelity worth flagging for review:
- A weaker later reason is NOT an error (design 348: "only a higher rank changes the target, no request removes a reason"), so upgradeDisposition unions it and leaves the target alone. The 49-pair sweep asserts the result equals max(rank) on every pair, so this cannot drift into an accidental downgrade.
- R5 leaves DRAINING only on adapter proof.
